newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pipeline planned from Amsterdam port to Schiphol.
newsitem.headline: Pipeline planned from Amsterdam port to Schiphol.

text.p: A plan to provide airlines at Schiphol airport in the Netherlands with a new pipeline carrying alternative supplies of aviation fuel has been put before local council planners for approval.

Aircraft Fuel Supply (AFS), a joint venture company co-owned by KLM and ten multinational oil companies, is seeking planning permission for a new 30 kilometre pipeline linking Schiphol and the port of Amsterdam.

A spokesman for the venture told Reuters in a telephone interview AFS has applied to the provincial council of North Holland, and the regional authorities of Haarlem and Amsterdam for permission to build the proposed pipeline.

The pipeline would, he said, provide an alternative to existing supplies of kerosene which currently arrive at the airport by barge via inland waterways, or by a former NATO pipeline link to Rotterdam.

The spokesman said the new pipeline could be built at a cost of 25 million guilders and could transport as much as two million tonnes of aviation fuel. It would link with existing storage facilities in the port of Amsterdam and connect to a distribution network at the east side of Schiphol airport.

AFS, which has been in existance at the airport for some 30 years, has, in addition to KLM, the following oil companies as shareholders: Mobil, Fina, Chevron, Exxon, Kuwait Oil Company, Elf, Total, British Petroleum Co Plc, Texaco and Shell. All eleven companies have 9.09% shares in the venture. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
